EXPERIMENT DESIGN DOCUMENT — CycleNet for forecasting time series with periodic patterns (design-only; no experiments run, no results claimed)

Source-marking convention used throughout: [K] = claim from researcher's prior knowledge of CycleNet (Lin et al., NeurIPS 2024, arXiv 2409.18479; official RRWCycleNet repo) — "per paper (unverified against workspace)"; [W] = verified workspace/environment observation; [A] = design assumption needing no external source.

1) GOAL AND HYPOTHESIS
Goal: show that a CycleNet-style model — a learnable, cyclically reused recurrent cycle component (RCF) combined with a simple residual forecast head — can be implemented and trained to forecast time series with explicit periodic patterns, and attribute any accuracy gain specifically to the RCF module.
H1 (primary): On periodic data, CycleNet-style (RCF + linear residual head) outperforms cycle-agnostic linear-family baselines (vanilla Linear, DLinear) at horizons aligned with the cycle.
H2 (attribution): The gain is attributable to the cyclic reuse of the learnable component: "CycleNet minus RCF" ablations (including the per-position non-reused bias added per researcher request) should lose most of the advantage, especially at horizons spanning ≥1 full cycle.
H3 (sensitivity): Performance degrades gracefully when the specified cycle length is mismatched (±1, ±half-cycle), consistent with the cycle length being a hyperparameter [K].
Falsification criteria: if the RCF model fails to beat naive seasonal on hourly synthetic weekly-cycle data, or the minus-RCF ablation matches full CycleNet within seed noise, H1/H2 are not supported.

2) CYCLENET MECHANICS (all [K] "per paper, unverified against workspace"; workspace contains only task.json [W])
- RCF: a learnable parameter Q of shape [cycle_length, n_channels], globally shared across the whole series, indexed cyclically (position t → Q[t mod C]). [K]
- Removal/restoration, two experimental branches (per researcher instruction):
  • Branch "Removal-first" (Forecast-with-RCF): subtract Q[t mod C] from the look-back window; forecast the residual with the head; add Q back at forecast positions. Loss on the residual or on the final output; Q is trained jointly. [K]
  • Branch "Restoration-style" (model-first): train the head on the raw series, subtract the model's cyclic prediction at training positions and fit Q to the cyclic remainder; predict = head output − Q-style correction at target positions. [K — described as the alternative training variant in the paper]
- Cycle length C: per-dataset hyperparameter from domain knowledge (hourly → 24 daily or 168 weekly); not estimated from data in the primary track. [K]
- Head: deliberately minimal — single Linear (main) or 1–2-layer MLP (variant); this is a "linear-family" model where RCF carries the signal. [K]
- Normalization: instance normalization (per-window mean/std computed on the look-back, inverted after restoration; RevIN-style). Channel-independent multivariate processing. [K]
- Decoding: direct multi-step (one shot per horizon) is primary; iterated/recurrent decoding is out of scope, see §8/limitations. [A per researcher instruction]

3) DATA — SYNTHETIC IS THE PRIMARY TRACK (per researcher instruction)
3.1 Synthetic generator (primary, fully reproducible offline):
For each channel i: y_i(t) = trend_i(t) + Σ_{k=1..K} A_ik · sin(2π·k·t/C_i + φ_i) + ε(t), with
- Base periods: C ∈ {24 (daily), 168 (weekly)}; multi-period series combine both harmonics.
- 3 harmonics with random amplitudes/phases per channel (fixed seed); optional slow linear trend; Gaussian noise with controllable SNR ∈ {high, medium, low}; optional random phase shift per channel; optional amplitude modulation (slow multiplicative envelope) to break perfect stationarity.
- Grid: n_channels ∈ {1 (univariate), 7, 21}; series length 10,000–20,000 steps; deterministic seeds so every model sees identical data.
- A "phase-shift stress set": same periodicity but the phase of the cycle shifts midway — probes robustness of a globally shared Q [A].
3.2 Real benchmarks (optional extension, only "if data are provided" — network is disabled [W]): Electricity (C=168), Traffic (C=168), Solar (C=24/144), Weather (C=24), ETT family (C=24); official chronological splits and look-backs [K]. Not required for the core deliverable.

4) MODELS, BASELINES, ABLATION MATRIX
All models share: direct multi-step linear-style mapping, instance norm [K], channel independence, identical look-back and loss.
M1 Full CycleNet (Removal-first branch), Linear head — primary model.
M2 Full CycleNet (Restoration-style branch) — second branch per researcher instruction.
M3 Head variant: M1 with MLP head.
M4 Ablation A (no RCF): instance norm + Linear head only (= DLinear-equivalent). Isolates "anything cyclic at all".
M5 Ablation B (static bias, no cycle structure): learnable scalar/vector bias per channel added to the forecast, never indexed by position. [per original design, retained]
M6 Ablation C (per-position non-reused bias — researcher's addition): learnable per-position bias of shape [look-back+horizon, C] trained per position WITHOUT cyclic reuse across windows. This separates "there is a trainable offset" (M5) from "the offset is cyclically recycled" (M1). If M6 ≈ M1 and both ≫ M4/M5, the gain is from cyclic reuse specifically; if M6 ≈ M1 but M5 fails, any trainable offset suffices — a discriminating outcome either way. [A]
M7 Naive seasonal baseline: ŷ(t+h) = y(t+h−C) — the must-beat periodic floor; and naive seasonal-drift variant.
Baselines beyond ablations: vanilla Linear (M4 covers it), DLinear [K]; optional full LTSF backbones (PatchTST/TimesNet) only if compute/data permit — not required.
Ablation matrix (run for every dataset × horizon × seed): {M1, M2, M3, M4, M5, M6, M7} = 7 models.

5) PROTOCOL
- Splits: chronological 60/20/20 (train/val/test) for synthetic; identical across all models; cycle-aligned boundaries where feasible (split points at multiples of C) [A].
- Normalization: z-score per channel using train statistics only; instance (per-window) norm inside the model per [K]; identical pipeline for every model; no leakage (val/test never touched by scaler fitting or cycle fitting).
- Horizons: {24, 48, 96, 168} for C=168 data; {12, 24, 48, 72} for C=24 data. Look-back: 336 default, 96 as a secondary (sensitivity to look-back ≥ C matters for RCF indexing).
- Seeds: ≥3 seeds per cell (report mean ± std); paired comparisons on identical data/splits.
- Metrics: MSE and MAE per horizon; per-channel MSE on multivariate; also "cycle-phase" breakdown (error by h mod C) to verify errors concentrate where the cycle is mis-specified [A]. Primary metric: test MSE at horizon = C (168 or 24), where cyclic reuse should matter most.
- Training: Adam, MSE loss (Huber as robustness variant [K]), early stopping on val MSE with fixed patience, fixed max epochs, identical batch size/LR schedule for all models; cycle length recorded per dataset.
- Success criterion (confirmation): M1 beats M4 and M5 beyond seed std at h=C on ≥2 of 3 main synthetic configurations, and beats naive seasonal on at least the high-SNR config; M6 discriminating result reported as in §4. Refutation: M1 ≤ naive seasonal or M6 ≈ M4 (no attributable gain).

6) ANALYSIS PLAN
- Attribution of the RCF gain: (a) paired deltas M1−M4, M1−M5, M1−M6 with per-seed bootstrap CIs; (b) phase-resolved error curves — if RCF works, errors at forecast positions should follow the cycle profile of Q, so plot learned Q against the true generative harmonic (synthetic advantage: ground-truth cycle is known — direct visual/quantitative recovery check, e.g., correlation between learned Q and generative A·sin terms per channel); (c) branch comparison M1 vs M2 to see whether removal-first vs restoration-style training matters [researcher's requested branch design].
- Cycle-length sensitivity: run M1 with C′ ∈ {C−1, C, C+1, C/2, 2C, 12 (mismatched)} on one representative synthetic config; expect a valley at C = true period [H3]. Also report behavior of a "wrong-period" naive seasonal as a control.
- Phase-shift stress: compare M1 vs M4 on the phase-shift set; a globally shared Q should degrade more — this is an honest potential negative result, reported as such.
- Univariate vs multivariate: main track multivariate channel-independent; univariate as a robustness slice (M1 vs M4 only, to bound compute).

7) FEASIBILITY (verified environment facts [W]: 224-core Xeon Platinum 8570, ~2 TB RAM, CPU-only, Python 3.14.4; torch, numpy, pandas NOT installed; no local wheel cache; network disabled)
- Compute estimate (minimal grid): 3 synthetic configs × 4 horizons × 3 seeds × 7 models ≈ 250 runs; linear-family models at look-back 336 are tiny (thousands of parameters); on CPU, ~1–5 min/run for training + seconds for baselines ⇒ roughly 10–20 CPU-hours serially, trivially parallelizable across 224 cores ⇒ wall-clock well under 1 hour if parallelized. Cycle-length sensitivity adds ~7 × 3 = 21 runs; phase-shift set ~2 × 4 × 3 = 24 runs. Total budget ≈ 300 runs, comfortably within one CPU day even serially.
- Key risks and mitigations:
  R1 (highest): no torch/numpy and no network ⇒ pip install impossible in this sandbox. Mitigations: (a) researcher provisions wheels/dependencies; (b) otherwise implement the linear models + Adam + synthetic generator in pure Python (feasible: models are linear; Adam and backprop for a linear layer are ~100 lines; slow but the grid is small — estimate ~5–10× slowdown, still feasible); (c) as last resort restrict to M1/M4/M7 (the minimum that still answers H1/H2).
  R2: Python 3.14.4 may lack compatible wheels even if provided. Mitigation: prefer pure-Python path or a supplied older-interpreter environment.
  R3: RCF details mis-recalled [K unverified]. Mitigation: both branches implemented (M1/M2) and all cycle/head/norm choices exposed as config flags, so a wrong recall changes one flag, not the design; document explicitly as "per paper (unverified)".
  R4: Phase-shift stress produces a negative result for CycleNet — acceptable, report honestly; the design's contribution is attribution, not advocacy.
  R5: Seed noise swallows small effects on low-SNR synthetic data. Mitigation: ≥3 seeds, bootstrap CIs, high-SNR config as the primary confirmation cell.
- Smoke tests actually permitted and performed during design: NONE beyond environment probes above (CPU count, RAM, package absence). Any future run must be labeled "shape checks, not experiments".

8) ASSUMPTIONS AND UNRESOLVED UNCERTAINTIES
Assumptions (explicitly not facts):
- A1: All CycleNet mechanics in §2 are correctly recalled from the paper/repo; per researcher instruction they are marked "per paper (unverified against workspace)" and cannot be confirmed from the workspace, which contains only task.json [W].
- A2: Cycle length is a hyperparameter (domain-given), with sensitivity scan secondary — not estimated from data.
- A3: Primary track is multivariate channel-independent with direct multi-step decoding; iterated/recurrent decoding is a limitations/future-work paragraph only (per researcher instruction): it changes error accumulation dynamics and could interact with RCF indexing, but is out of scope for this design.
- A4: Synthetic data with known generative cycles is an acceptable and sufficient basis for answering the research question; real benchmarks are an optional extension.
- A5: Budget is the minimal grid of §7 unless the researcher enlarges it; CPU-only execution is accepted, including the pure-Python contingency if dependencies cannot be provisioned.
Unresolved uncertainties:
- U1: The exact removal-vs-restoration formulation and loss placement in the original paper cannot be verified here; both branches are implemented, but neither is claimed to be the canonical one.
- U2: No researcher-supplied datasets exist; if real data later arrives, split/look-back conventions must be matched to the official benchmark protocol [K], which may shift absolute numbers relative to published results.
- U3: Whether the researcher requires exact reproduction of published CycleNet numbers (unlikely, given synthetic primary track) or only the attribution experiment (assumed).
- U4: Dependency provisioning (torch/numpy wheels) is outside my control; the pure-Python fallback path is designed but its runtime estimate is approximate.
